title: Korea to Invest Up to $120B in 8 US Reactors, Pursues Westinghouse Stake
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · October 1, 2026

Korea and the U.S. agreed to a framework under which Korea would invest up to $120 billion to help build eight large nuclear reactors on U.S. soil, including two Korean-model APR1400 units, while Korean entities also pursue a 5–10% equity stake in Westinghouse. Here is what the two governments announced and what is still subject to case-by-case approval.

CompanyRoleEvidence
KEPCO
KRX: 015760		Potential Westinghouse equity investor; construction and equipment supply chain participantReported (joint Korea-U.S. announcement, Oct 1, 2026)
KHNP (Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power)APR1400 reactor builder/operator; potential Westinghouse equity investorReported
Westinghouse (U.S.)AP1000 reactor supplier; target of Korean equity stake talksReported

What was announced

  • The deal: Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy published a joint U.S.-Korea press release and fact sheet on October 1 outlining "Project Power," under which Korea would invest up to $120 billion toward building eight large reactors in the U.S. — two APR1400 units (Korea's own design) and six Westinghouse AP1000 units.
  • Funding split: of the $120 billion, $100 billion is earmarked for reactor construction and $20 billion as a contingency reserve for cost overruns.
  • Early payment: Korea is pursuing advance payment of up to $10 billion by year-end to lock in long-lead-time equipment orders, contingent on meeting domestic legal requirements.
  • Agreement amendment: KEPCO and KHNP plan to amend their existing settlement with Westinghouse (reached last year to end an intellectual property dispute), which currently restricts APR1400 construction in the U.S., to carve out an exception allowing the two APR1400 units in this project.
  • Equity stake: the government is reviewing a plan for KEPCO, KHNP and private Korean companies to acquire a 5–10% stake in Westinghouse, aiming to expand Korean firms' role in construction and equipment supply for Westinghouse's AP1000 projects both in the U.S. and internationally.

What is not yet confirmed

Investment in all eight reactors is not finalized. The two governments still need to work out site selection, construction schedules, project structure and commercial terms before deciding whether to proceed with each individual project based on its commercial merits. (Reported)

Why the Westinghouse agreement matters

Trade Minister Kim Jung-kwan said at a background briefing last month that the framework includes amending the settlement specifically so two APR1400 units can be built in the U.S. Under the current agreement, APR1400 construction in the U.S. is restricted; without the amendment, Korea's own reactor design could not be part of this project at all.

Quick FAQ

Is the $120 billion investment confirmed?
Not entirely. It is a joint framework agreement; final investment decisions for each of the eight reactors depend on site, schedule, and commercial terms still to be worked out.

Why does Korea need to amend its Westinghouse agreement?
A settlement reached last year to end an IP dispute currently restricts Korea from building APR1400 reactors in the U.S. The amendment carves out an exception for the two APR1400 units in this project.

Has a Westinghouse stake purchase been finalized?
No. The government is reviewing a plan for KEPCO, KHNP and private companies to acquire a 5–10% stake; no deal has been announced as signed.
